files.summary: reconcile starter and packing defaults, public health and superseded recovery bounds
edits: **Deferred integration:** this inventory describes the pinned review branch. [Lifecycle and protection](../worlds/base/lifecycle-and-protection.md) identifies the newer accepted player danger/death rules and their pinned main implementation. Main’s [FT01–FT07 inventory](https://github.com/Macrofold/OpenLegend/blob/0a3ab79b7a698a7f1941dc23722f89220d1ba425/docs/limits/base-world.md#ft01--proposed-first-threat-scope-and-reward) owns their exact encounter, reincarnation and simulated-fade bounds. The older collapse/recovery values below are baseline observations, not the accepted integration target or evidence qualifying the newer rules.

initial bundled items and ordinary primitive invention outputs use **1 packing unit**. Generated containers instead use their family’s [derived capacity and own-load rule](../worlds/base/camp-containers.md#first-family-rules); the primitive default is not a uniform load for every future output

older review baseline’s installed body policy uses player collapse versus other-controller death. Its living-player recovery requires collapse, health below 30% or food below 20, plus a valid walkable safe-return point; floors are health 65%, food 45 and energy 65. Creator revival separately fills raw maximum health and configured applicable meters; ordinary health edits never revive a dead body. Health/energy concerns are instant, without extra notices. Compact bars use the rounded displayed value at or below 20; creator-editor critical thresholds remain strict below 40/30/25. Consumption and prompt language read this policy and meter definitions. [Recorded baseline evidence](../verification/world-configured-survival.md) preserves that earlier human behavior and proves proportional thresholds on a 36-point body; it does not qualify the later selected death/reincarnation rules.
